cards.text: Micah, the prophet, passes along what the LORD says, and friend, it sounds like a courtroom. Somebody is told to arise and plead a case before the mountains and let the hills hear. Then the mountains themselves get called "you enduring foundations of the earth."

cards.question: True or false: the LORD's case in front of the mountains is against the nations.

cards.text: The LORD's case is against His own people, Israel. He opens with a question, and I bet you could hear a crumb drop: "My people, what have I done to you?"

cards.question: After asking His people what He has done to them, what does the LORD dare them to testify about?

answers.text: How they have kept His laws
Who they trust more than Him

cards.text: Then the LORD reminds them He brought them up from the land of Egypt and redeemed them from the house of slavery. Friend, He pulled ME out of a junk drawer, and I tell that story to ANYBODY who stands still for five seconds.

cards.question: Moses, Israel's leader, had a brother and a sister (Numbers 26:59). The LORD says He sent Moses before His people, as well as Aaron and ___.

cards.text: Next, the LORD says to remember Balak, king of Moab, who sent for Balaam, son of Beor, to curse Israel (Numbers 22:5-6). Balaam blessed them instead, THREE TIMES, like hiring a guy to trash-talk your rival and he just keeps hyping him up (Numbers 24:10).

Then He says to remember the journey from Shittim to Gilgal, across the Jordan (Joshua 3:1; 4:19). Friend, on most trips the only thing that stops is traffic, but on THAT trip the Jordan stopped (Joshua 3:16).

cards.question: Why does the LORD want His people to remember Balaam and the journey to Gilgal?

answers.text: So they'll see the LORD is righteous
So they'll keep far away from Moab
So they'll never trust a foreign king

cards.question: Then the passage asks, "With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high?" True or false: the first offering it wonders about bringing is a burnt offering.

cards.text: Then the questions get BIGGER: would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, or ten thousand rivers of oil? Friend, I tossed one extra scoop of chocolate chips in a batch once and walked around all week like a HERO.
Then the questions go somewhere heavy: "Shall I present my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"

cards.question: True or false: after all those questions about offerings, the passage says no one has been shown what is good.
The passage says, "He has shown you, O man, what is good." So what does it say the LORD requires?

answers.text: Justice and mercy and a humble walk with Him
More and bigger offerings at every feast
A long trip up to the temple every year
